before.content:
<!-- layout: title; theme: keynote; design: v1 -->
# The intake pilot

A shorter review cycle, with an unanswered quality question. [1][2]

---

<!-- layout: composed -->
<!-- scene:  -->
## The pilot measured time; quality remains unknown [1][2]

In this synthetic intake pilot, median review time was 40 hours before the pilot and 16 hours during the pilot. The observation covered two teams over eight weeks. These are training data, not actual organizational results. [1]

The two-team intake pilot did not measure review quality or error rates. A faster review cannot establish a quality improvement. The sample does not establish an effect in other teams. [2]

findings.problem: The reference marker [1] wraps onto a line of its own below "These are training data, not actual organizational results.", leaving a stray bracketed character stranded at the left margin and adding a ragged extra line.
findings.correction: Keep the marker attached to the sentence it supports: shorten the paragraph slightly, widen the text column, or make the citation a non-breaking unit so [1] stays on the last line of the paragraph.

findings.problem: The headline result (40 hours before, 16 hours during) sits inside a dense 32pt paragraph with no visual emphasis, so the time result the slide is about does not stand out for decision-makers.
findings.correction: Pull the two numbers into a simple before/after contrast element or bold them within the sentence so the 40h → 16h change is legible at a glance, without adding claims beyond the source.
